title: Foundational transcript analysis: 2016 plus 2017 Essence of Calculus
method: Read all substantive sentence_timings.json content for every assigned nonempty file. No videos or frames watched. Analysis is of narrated visual instructions and reasoning, not verified rendered staging. Timings are source-caption seconds, rounded here to one decimal. Broad coding was manual after full reading; regex keyword hits were not substituted for reading.
cautions: 2016/hanoi-and-sierpinski has interleaved/duplicated/midword fragments and 21 nonpositive intervals; many final segments collapse to 838.1 seconds. Its rhetorical content is usable cautiously, but timing/ordering and raw word totals are unreliable.
2016/determinant contains a reversed 178.2–177.0 interval and repeated adjacent text. 2017/higher-order-derivatives contains duplicated/interleaved text and reversed 245.2–244.2 interval.

Other transcripts contain transcription errors in formula language. This is style research, not mathematical verification; equations and historical/physical claims must not be silently endorsed by quoting the captions.

Raw elapsed transcript span includes pauses, non-explanatory sections, thanks and sponsorship, and cannot establish speaking rate or video duration. Gaps cannot establish silence, reading holds, or animation lengths without audiovisual checks.
Deliberate choreography, color persistence, and gaze guidance are reported only where the narration explicitly describes them; effectiveness and actual motion execution remain unverified.
Quoted text budget is under 25 words per individual video across this report. Inventory descriptions are paraphrases.
